transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE); Jacob Liu (Redwood SE); Priya Rao (Ledgerly - Lead Backend Eng); Ethan Smith (Ledgerly - PM); Marta Gomez (Ledgerly - ML Eng)
Shared artifacts: https://drive.redwood/pilot/ledgerly/sdk-invocation.md, shared deck: https://drive.redwood/pilot/ledgerly/deck-v2.pdf

Summary (auto): quick sync on SDK behavior for function-calling and structured output; reviewed failure modes from last week's runs (schema mismatches, streaming truncation, token overrun); decided SDK snippet updates + targeted tests.

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): All right everyone, thanks for joining, hope holiday week hasn't slowed things too much. Quick agenda: Jacob will walk through the SDK changes we pushed, then we'll review the failures you uploaded, then next steps.
[00:18] Priya (Ledgerly): Yep thanks, we have a handful of logs and the sample payloads in the folder. We started seeing two main issues: 1) the function-calling responses sometime omit optional fields, and 2) streaming responses cut off mid-json when we try to parse on the fly.
[00:35] Jacob (Redwood SE): Got it, yea we've been triaging. The optional field omission is usually the model not emitting the key when it decides the value is empty; that interacts weirdly with your strict parser. We have a couple of strategies: explicit schema-enforcement in the SDK that injects defaults, or post-parse reconciliation.
[00:52] Ethan (PM): Can you explain the default injection? We don't want hidden defaults changing behavior silently.
[01:05] Jacob (Redwood SE): Totally. The idea is the SDK exposes a "schema.mode" flag: strict | permissive | defaults. In defaults mode it will add null or empty-array fields when missing, with a clear annotation in the metadata header so your app can detect injected values. It's not magic — it's a wrapper step after the function call result arrives.
[01:28] Marta (Ledgerly): That could work. But second issue is streaming: when we stream token-by-token and parse as we go, occasionally the JSON chunk boundary is mid-structure and our incremental parser throws. Some of those were network jitter but others look like the runtime's chunking behavior.
[01:50] Jacob (Redwood SE): Right, there's two related layers: the runtime sends events for token batches; the SDK provides an incremental JSON assembly helper. We found cases where nested arrays—like a list of line items with optional metadata—produce deeply nested partial buffers. Our fix is to buffer until a valid JSON root is seen or until a timeout threshold, plus expose a streaming callback that gives you both "raw_chunk" and "assembled_object" events.
[02:12] Priya (Ledgerly): Buffering until root detection sounds ok, but we need guarantees for latency — our UX depends on first-item arrival under 300ms. Will buffering add noticeable latency?
[02:30] Jacob (Redwood SE): We added heuristics: immediate emit for top-level keys that are complete, otherwise buffer only for nested structures up to 200ms. In practice on our internal tests median added latency was ~40ms for nested-heavy outputs. But yes, you'd see slightly longer tail.
[02:50] Sofia (AE): Wanted to flag, Lydia on infra asked about KV cache effect here — if prefixes are cached, do you see different tokenization or structure?
[03:04] Jacob (Redwood SE): Good question. KV cache is orthogonal — it affects generation continuity, not the structural output. But we saw one case where cached prefix led model to drop optional block because context indicated repetition. That is more of a prompt engineering / cache-invalid-before-generation issue.
[03:23] Ethan (PM): Ok makes sense. On the logs we uploaded, there were also 2 examples where the function call resolved to a different function name than expected — it returned "summarize_transactions" vs our expected "format_transactions". Is that a model routing problem?
[03:40] Marta (ML Eng): Those looked like semantically similar functions; the model sometimes picks the closest function signature. We concrete-ized the signatures but there's still overlap. We need to tighten the function descriptions or use stricter name anchors.
[03:57] Jacob (Redwood SE): Yup, SDK supports function disambiguation by passing an explicit function_id and also enabling a "require_exact_name" flag which will return an error if the model picks the wrong function — that fails fast so you don't get silently different behavior.
[04:15] Priya (Ledgerly): That fail-fast mode — does it count as an error in metrics (affects success rate) and how are those surfaced in the console?
[04:27] Jacob (Redwood SE): It surfaces as a function mismatch error in the SDK metrics; in Console you'll see per-route breakdowns with error category "function_mismatch" and a sample log. We can also flag those as non-billing in the POC if you prefer.
[04:40] Sofia (AE): On the cost side, Marta had a question about token churn from repeated partial calls during retries.
[04:50] Marta (Ledgerly): Yeah we saw retries when function mismatch turned into fallback calls; the token cost doubled in worst cases. Can Redwood make retries conservative?
[05:03] Jacob (Redwood SE): The SDK supports a retry policy — you can set max_retries and a "retry_when" predicate. For function mismatch I'd recommend 0-1 retries with the require_exact_name flag to avoid blind retries. Also we added a "dry-run" mode to capture what would have been called without consuming billable tokens — handy for testing.
[05:25] Ethan (PM): Nice. About structured outputs — we sent a case where nested arrays contained nulls and empty arrays; the downstream service threw because it expected at least one object.
[05:38] Priya (Ledgerly): Correct, the JSON schema in our processor has required>1 in that array. Is there a way to force model to include at least one placeholder item when uncertain?
[05:52] Jacob (Redwood SE): Two levers — 1) prompt-level instruction to include placeholder when empty (explicit template), 2) SDK post-processor to auto-insert a sentinel object with metadata.explain = "auto-inserted". We prefer keeping it explicit in prompt for predictability but SDK sentinel gives you safety net.
[06:12] Priya (Ledgerly): Hmm prompt fix means we have to version prompts and watch cost. SDK sentinel seems low-risk for compatibility.
[06:22] Jacob (Redwood SE): We can make sentinel optional and annotated; your downstream can filter it with a flag.
[06:30] Sofia (AE): Quick pause — Marta you had results from the regression harness?
[06:38] Marta (Ledgerly): Yes, I ran 500 sample prompts across the three models you suggested. Failures: 12% schema mismatch, 5% truncated streams, 2% wrong function. Latency median 220ms for hosted route, p95 620ms. Token cost averaged 1.8x our baseline model. Full CSV is in the shared folder.
[06:58] Jacob (Redwood SE): Thanks. The 12% is higher than we like. Can you point to a couple of representative transcripts?
[07:08] Marta (Ledgerly): Uploaded files named fail_schema_01...03 — I can open one now.
[07:15] [07:15] Marta (Ledgerly): (reading) here's an example where model omitted "merchant_details" entirely, we had a parser crash.
[07:25] Jacob (Redwood SE): Okay that matches the missing-key issue. Quick mitigation: enable schema.mode=defaults plus the streaming buffer; also add require_exact_name on function calls — that should drop those categories to single digits. We'll follow up with a patch to SDK snippets.
[07:40] Priya (Ledgerly): Another operational ask — audit logs. Our security team wants every function call and its resolved arguments stored for 90 days with KMS-wrapped keys. Can Redwood support that in Private or Dedicated?
[07:56] Sofia (AE): Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and 90-day retention; Dedicated has configurable retention too. We'll send the security pack (SOC2/ISO) and an example audit log schema.
[08:10] Ethan (PM): Can we get an example log export? We want to ingest into Splunk.
[08:18] Jacob (Redwood SE): Sure — we'll include a sample event format: {"timestamp":...,"route":...,"function_invoked":...,"args":...,"decision":...} — note args can be redacted per config.
[08:34] Priya (Ledgerly): Great. One more question: when streaming + function-calling, if a function is triggered mid-stream, how does the SDK handle the partial buffer?
[08:47] Jacob (Redwood SE): The SDK will emit a "stream_interruption" event with raw chunks and then call the function with the assembled argument buffer. If the buffer isn't complete, we provide a confidence score and optional retry logic. There's also a mode to pause streaming until function completes.
[09:05] Marta (Ledgerly): Confidence scoring — is that model-backed or heuristic?
[09:12] Jacob (Redwood SE): Heuristic currently (chunk completeness, bracket balancing) plus a light FFNN that learned from our internal logs for likely-complete detection. We can tune for your dataset if you share annotated examples.
[09:28] Priya (Ledgerly): We'll share annotations for 50-100 examples.
[09:34] Sofia (AE): Perfect. Back to next steps — Jacob, you'll drop that SDK code snippet and also a short readme on configuration knobs. Priya/Marta you'll run the 3 edge-case tests and drop results. Sofia to schedule next sync.
[09:52] Ethan (PM): Rough timeline — we can get tests done by Jan 8 and review the week after.
[09:58] Sofia (AE): Sounds good. Any blockers?
[10:02] Priya (Ledgerly): Only security signoff timeline; otherwise good.
[10:08] Jacob (Redwood SE): I'll also throw in a quick sample for "require_exact_name" and the sentinel object so you can toggle easily.
[10:18] Marta (Ledgerly): One tiny nit — in your example links, the SDK snippet references method names that don't match our internal naming. We'll align names in the sample code.
[10:28] Jacob (Redwood SE): Good catch, we'll parametrize names in the snippet.
[10:34] Sofia (AE): Okay final recap: Jacob send SDK snippet + streaming notes + sample log format by 2026-01-06; Priya/Marta run edge-case tests and upload by 2026-01-08; Sofia schedule follow-up for week of 2026-01-13.
[10:51] Ethan (PM): Thanks everyone.
[10:54] Priya (Ledgerly): Thanks.
[10:56] Sofia (AE): End.

Action items (auto): Jacob to create updated SDK example; Priya/Marta to run edge-case tests; Sofia to send calendar invite for follow-up.
